input.quote: In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 gives either Party a convenience exit on ninety (90) days' written notice, which satisfies the fallback notice elements for both sides. It fails the fallback on two material terms. First, because the terminating Party's notice simply "shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated", HDI's termination is not tied to the end of the then-current one-year term and operates as a mid-term walk-away. Second, our exit is penalised by an uncapped Termination Payment (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000), far exceeding the three-months-of-fees cap. We therefore target the fallback with the two shortest conforming edits: an HDI Termination Date fixed at the end of the then-current term, and a three-month fee cap on the Termination Payment (the existing zero-floor in 4.2(b) and the quarterly instalment mechanic in 4.2(c) remain workable under the cap).

proposal.summary: Cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees and limit HDI's termination to the end of the then-current term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can live with the mutual ninety (90) days' notice, but not with an uncapped exit payment or an HDI walk-away mid-term: we cap the Termination Payment at three months of fees and require any HDI-specified Termination Date to fall at the end of the then-current term.
